33. Alkenes are more reactive than alkanes. Give reason. Answer: Alkenes are more reactive than alkanes because they contain a carbon–carbon double bond (C=C) which has a weak π-bond.
Explanation: The π-bond present in alkenes is less stable. This bond breaks easily and takes part in addition reactions. Alkanes have only strong single (σ) bonds, so they are less reactive.

34. The IUPAC system of nomenclature is preferred for naming hydrocarbons. Give reason. Answer: The IUPAC system is preferred because it provides a systematic and universally accepted method of naming hydrocarbons.
Explanation: Each compound has only one unique name. The name indicates structure and carbon chain length. It avoids confusion caused by common names.
35. Condensed formulas are often used in organic chemistry. Give reason.
Answer: Condensed formulas are used because they are short, simple, and easy to write.
Explanation: They show the arrangement of atoms clearly.
SEE Chemistry – Give Reasons (Q.33–37) They save time and space while writing reactions. They are convenient for large organic molecules.

36. Alcohols are considered derivatives of hydrocarbons. Give reason. Answer: Alcohols are derivatives of hydrocarbons because one hydrogen atom of a hydrocarbon is replaced by a hydroxyl (–OH) group.
Explanation: Example: Ethane (C₂H₆) → Ethanol (C₂H₅OH). The carbon chain remains unchanged.

37. Ethyl alcohol (ethanol) is commonly used as a disinfectant and fuel. Give reason. Answer: Ethanol is used as a disinfectant because it kills germs, and as a fuel because it burns easily to produce heat.
Explanation: 70% ethanol destroys bacterial and viral cell membranes. It burns with a clean flame and releases energy.
